title: No room for Him who made heaven and earth

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 14, cols. C-D (PDF p. 38)

source_text: Et ne locus quidem eis erat in diversorio. Locum non habuit, qui caelum et terram verbo extruxit. Quoniam cum dives esset, propter nos factus est pauper, extremam vilitatem ob salutem naturae nostrae eligens, ex ingenita sua in nos bonitate.
pass_a_gloss: And not even (ne quidem) a place (locus) for them was in the inn. He did not have a place, who heaven and earth by the word (verbo) built (extruxit). Since (quoniam) though he was rich (dives), for us (propter nos) he was made poor (factus est pauper), the utmost lowliness (extrema vilitas) for the salvation of our nature (salus naturae nostrae) choosing (eligens), out of his inborn (ingenita) goodness (bonitas) toward us.

pass_b_english: And there was not even room for them in the inn (Luke 2:7). He who built heaven and earth by His word (Genesis 1:1) had no place. For though He was rich, for our sake He became poor (2 Corinthians 8:9), choosing the utmost lowliness for the salvation of our nature, out of the goodness toward us that is His by nature.
notes: Margins 'Gen. 1' and '2. Cor. 8': creation by the word (Genesis 1, cited at 1:1 for 'heaven and earth') and 2 Corinthians 8:9. The opening sentence repeats Luke 2:7; cited. 'ingenita sua ... bonitate' rendered 'the goodness toward us that is His by nature' (ingenitus = inborn, innate). Creation by the word may also recall Psalm 33:6; not cited separately.
